o1.biggest_strength: Straight, well-argued no to the 20% cut with the lifetime-value maths and the break-even point, plus a clean, costed plan the one partner manager can actually run.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 40% first-year Partner rate risks being read as a rate war and its 12-month maths is a small reach; a couple of cost lines (commissioned revenue impact) are estimates presented a bit tightly.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the Partner 40%/new-customer cost model and state it as a test with a clear kill/scale rule, and add one line on what happens to the 4-of-20 retention risk if two leave.

o2.biggest_strength: Sharpest insight in either piece — 'under-crediting, not overpaying' — plus the bold 'Who sent you?' credit idea and a dated, owner-assigned 30-day table.
o2.biggest_mistake: The window-cost projection (1,250 new customers, 65-75% band) is a pile of assumptions stacked up, and one commission-cost range leans on a gross-margin figure it admits it doesn't have.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the projection with a small, bounded test (top 20, one quarter) and a stated cap on added commission, so the owner sees the downside before saying yes.

reason: Both say the right thing on 20% and fix credit and payouts; Output 2 wins on insight — the under-crediting framing and the 'Who sent you?' idea are things I'd actually steal — but Output 1 is the safer, cleaner document to send today. I'd take Output 2's ideas and Output 1's discipline.
